subject: Renewal: segmented usage splits & discount asks
messages:
From: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@novusai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novusai.com
Date: 2027-08-01T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — usage split and discount request

Hi Logan,

Now that our annual term is coming up (end of August), procurement asked me to reach out early so we can avoid last-minute churn. I attached our Q2 token usage by product (Novus_Q2_usage.csv) — you can see heavy spikes on the embedding pipeline in May/Jun and more steady chat generation.

Two asks from our side: 1) can Redwood support a segmented commit where embeddings and chat get different per-token bands (we expect chat to grow faster), and 2) we need a clearer cap on renewal uplift so finance can model worst-case. Our procurement team is uncomfortable with unrestricted uplift above last-year usage.

High-level numbers: current rolling monthly avg ~700M tokens, peak months ~1.4B. We are evaluating a 12 month commit and would prefer a soft-commit option for the first quarter if possible.

Can you propose a path (bands, uplift cap, true-up cadence) and an initial modeled price? Also please include legal/procurement expectations for DocuSign timing — we target sign by Aug 20.

Thanks,
Kevin
Head of ML 
NovusAI

[Attachment: Novus_Q2_usage.csv (csv)]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@novusai.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — usage split and discount request

Kevin — appreciate the data and the early heads-up. Attached a quick pricing matrix (redwood_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx) showing one way to split commits across two buckets: chat gen and embeddings. Key proposal highlights:

- Segmented bands: Chat tiered at 0-500M / 500M-1.25B / >1.25B; Embeddings tiered at 0-250M / 250M-750M / >750M.
- Per-token discounts: incremental scale for higher bands (sample: 8% / 14% / 20% on hosted per-token list).
- Soft-commit option: first 3 months shelter where overage recognized but true-up deferred (helps you ramp).
- Renewal uplift cap: we can offer a contractual uplift limit (ceiling on per-token increase relative to prior term) — preliminary: 25% cap on list price movement for committed bands.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups with a trailing 3-month smoothing for burst months.

If that aligns, Priyom / Lauren will put together a draft term sheet and propose language for uplift ceilings + burst smoothing.

Will also include a DocuSign timeline — we can do a two-week review period and aim for execution by Aug 20 if legal is comfortable.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@novusai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — usage split and discount request

Kevin / Logan — thanks. I pulled together a short term-sheet draft and an example calc to show how the segmented bands affect effective per-token price at different run rates (attached redwood_draft_term_sheet_v2.pdf). A few notes and asks:

- Proposed params (example): 12-month commitment, 15% baseline discount at commit floor, additional incremental discounts as you hit higher band thresholds; per-token ceilings for burst months at 1.5x the committed rate to limit cost shock.
- Uplift cap: we prefer keeping the cap tied to list-price movement rather than effective blended price; that helps preserve discounts tied to volume. We can move the cap to 20% for Novus as a compromise, with a 3-month smoothing window to absorb spikes.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-up (within 30 days of quarter close) with a one-time annual true-up reconciliation.

Question for you: do you need per-region (US/EU) splits in the commit or is a single global commit acceptable for Novus? If you operate in EU and need separate commitments for compliance/latency, we can model that as a two-line commit.

Linking the HubSpot record for visibility: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

If these parameters look reasonable I will circulate the language and a DocuSign-ready term sheet.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Renewals, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_draft_term_sheet_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@novusai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novusai.com, Sarah Ng <sarah.legal@novusai.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T15:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — usage split and discount request

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful. A few clarifications from procurement/legal:

- Uplift cap: 20% is closer to acceptable, but we want explicit language about exceptions for extraordinary events (we'll ask for a 30-day notice if you invoke an exception).
- Burst protection: the 1.5x per-token ceiling is acceptable, but procurement is asking for a 3-month smoothing rule so one flash spike doesn't push us into a higher band permanently.
- True-up: quarterly true-ups are fine; however, our finance team prefers monthly reporting exports so they can monitor against the committed bands. Can you commit to a monthly usage CSV export (automated)?
- SLA credits: want to confirm limited credits if latency SLOs are missed during peak processing windows — can we get specifics?

Finally, legal has a tight DocuSign window and asked if we can do sign-off steps in parallel (commercial first, legal second) to hit the Aug 20 date. If Redwood can lock commercial terms and start the DocuSign flow today, we'll prioritize legal review.

Kevin

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@novusai.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final commercial path for execution (draft term sheet attached)

Kevin / team — looping in a short, executable path so procurement/legal can start parallel review:

- Commercial compromise: 12-month commitment, segmented bands as proposed, 20% uplift cap on list price movement, and a 3-month smoothing window for burst months.
- Burst ceiling: 1.5x per-token cap for any calendar month above 1.5x your 3-month rolling average; those excess tokens will be charged at the capped rate and included in the next quarterly true-up.
- True-up cadence: quarterly reconciliation with monthly automated usage CSV feed to your finance mailbox (we'll provide a push subscription to exports).
- SLA credits: limited credits tied to P99 latency thresholds during normal traffic; if you want the detailed SLO table I'll add it to the term sheet.
- Execution: attached a DocuSign-ready term sheet. If you confirm commercial terms in this thread I will send for signatures and mark legal review as the parallel step. We can target Aug 20 execution if signatories are ready.

Next steps: Kevin — confirm you accept the 20% uplift cap + 3-month smoothing and we will initiate the DocuSign flow today. If procurement needs a slightly different burst definition, tell us now and we can adjust the term sheet before sending.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Renewals Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_draft_term_sheet_v2.pdf (pdf)]
